source_revision_relation: direct ancestor of HEAD; HEAD adds the coordinator's withdraw/enforce commit and this dispatch. Source-only, so the delta cannot affect a number.

proposed_active_bridge.description: NXP TEA2209T/1 active-bridge-rectifier controller driving a four-MOSFET synchronous full bridge at the PFC input, replacing the incumbent U1 passive GBJ2510-F bridge. The proposal is AR-DESIGN/AR-VERIFY attempt-001 (this is the design the task says to assess); it is NOT on the retained board.
proposed_active_bridge.reference_mosfet: IPW60R017C7, Infineon 600 V CoolMOS C7, Final Data Sheet Rev. 2.0, 2016-03-01
proposed_active_bridge.topology: two devices conduct in the line path per half-cycle (one high side, one low side); high side driven from a bootstrap floating supply (VCCHL/VCCHR), low side from VCC; body diodes form a passive bridge at start-up and whenever the drivers are off
proposed_active_bridge.reference_hot_rds_basis: AR-DESIGN/AR-VERIFY computed Tj 45-46 C, typical curve; not a guaranteed hot maximum

controller_behaviour_under_fault.operation: senses mains polarity at L/R (+/-250 mV comparator) and switches diagonal device pairs on/off; has no current sensing and no overcurrent protection
protections_present: 8.3.1 gate pull-down: on driver-supply UVLO the gate output is discharged to <2 V

8.3.2 power-MOSFET drain-source protection: if Vds exceeds VVCC-2 V (low side) or VVCCHL/VCCHR-3.5 V (high side), all gate driver outputs are disabled; the documented purpose is to avoid high dissipation and high current peaks during start-up
8.3.3 minimum mains voltage: the charge state is entered only when |L| or |R| > 22 V
external disable only via the COMP pin
protections_absent: no short-circuit or desaturation trip on the power devices
no fault output / no shoot-through latch
no way to open a body-diode path
controller_behaviour_under_fault.behaviour_on_a_shorted_external_device: cannot detect or isolate it; gate shutdown leaves the body diode conducting, so all-drivers-off reverts the bridge to the passive diode bridge and the fault path persists

fault_path_assessment.line_fed_path: mains L -> F1 -> CMC U3 -> NTC U4 / bypass relay U5 -> active-bridge AC terminal (L or R) -> conducting diagonal pair -> VR/plus -> boost inductor U8 -> shorted U9 -> PFC_BUS_MINUS -> shunt U12 -> bridge return minus -> active-bridge complementary device -> AC terminal -> CMC -> mains N
fault_path_assessment.structural_effect_vs_passive_bridge: the active bridge is in the same series position as the passive bridge, so it cannot open the line-fed loop either; because it conducts through MOSFET channels (low Rds) instead of ~2 diode drops, it LOWERS the fault-loop limiting impedance and raises the prospective fault current for the same (unknown) line impedance. It makes interruption MORE dependent on F1, not less.
fault_path_assessment.active_bridge_specific_new_fault: a single active-bridge MOSFET failing short creates a line-fed short on the opposite half-cycle through that device and the complementary body diode; the TEA2209T has no overcurrent detection, so it cannot identify or isolate it, and a shorted device also defeats the diagonal-pair dead time
fault_path_assessment.voltage_stress: on a boost-diode short the bus is placed on the bridge output (~400 V, AR-FAULT corrected result); on a boost-switch short the devices see the line peak (186.7 V at 132 Vrms). 400 V is inside the 600 V device and the 440 V controller operating limit; voltage is NOT the binding fault stress. The active-bridge voltage rating remains gated by the undeclared surge clamp (AR-DESIGN/AR-VERIFY), separate from this fault.

mosfet_survival_evidence.id_pulse_note: pulse width limited by Tj,max; a single-pulse rating, NOT an IFSM
mosfet_survival_evidence.i2t_note: no I2t rating is published for this MOSFET
mosfet_survival_evidence.soa: Datasheet Diagrams 2 and 3 (Safe operating area) and Diagram 4 (max transient thermal impedance) exist but are raster figures whose coordinates were not digitised for this attempt (AR-DESIGN digitised only Diagrams 7, 8, 10)
mosfet_survival_evidence.survival_why: requires the prospective fault current (line impedance unresolved) AND the fault duration (F1 total clearing unresolved) to map onto the SOA/Zth curves; both are null. The incumbent GBJ passive bridge's 350 A IFSM / 510 A2s I2t cannot be used to qualify this replacement.
mosfet_survival_evidence.cannot_be_qualified_by: the GBJ passive bridge's IFSM 350 A / I2t 510 A2s

fault_classes.name: Line-fed switch short
fault_classes.limiting_impedance: AC source/line impedance + CMC + NTC/bypass + wiring + the conducting device channels; the AC source/line impedance is NOT established, so the limiting impedance is unknown
fault_classes.timescale: ms class; a 60 Hz half-cycle is 8.333 ms and F1 (16 A time-lag) clears in ms to 10s of ms at these currents
fault_classes.interrupting_element: F1 (Schurter 0034.3129, 16 A / 250 V time-lag, holder U2) is the only series interrupting element in this loop; its coordination is UNESTABLISHED
fault_classes.why_null: the AC source/line impedance is not established, so the prospective current is unknown; F1 total clearing behaviour at matching conditions is not captured

fault_classes.name: Internal capacitor discharge
examples: shorted boost diode U10 with the boost switch U9 conducting
fault_classes.loop: capacitors (PFC_BUS_PLUS_390V) -> shorted U10 -> a1 -> U9 -> capacitors (PFC_BUS_MINUS)
fault_classes.stored_energy_basis: 0.5*C*V^2 at the 400 V bus setpoint; equal voltage across the parallel bank
fault_classes.timescale_note: ~100 us class; R_loop * C with R_loop taken as the boost-switch Rds_on(typ) 42 mOhm ONLY, because the shunt is not in this loop (the withdrawn 116 us figure wrongly included the 10 mOhm shunt)
fault_classes.limiting_impedance: boost switch channel Rds_on + the shorted SiC boost diode's forward characteristic at multi-kA + bank ESR + layout; not defensibly modelled at multi-kA
fault_classes.interrupting_element_note: F1 is not in this loop; the shunt U12 has only one terminal on the loop; the PFC controller UCC28180D observes bus voltage and the shunt, neither of which is in this loop; gate shutdown cannot open a shorted U10 or a conducting U9 channel
fault_classes.why_null: no defensible model exists for the loop impedance over a multi-kA SiC-diode discharge; the split depends on the diode Vf(I), Rds(Tj), EST and layout, none of which is established

line_fed_switch_short.acting_element: F1 Schurter 0034.3129 time-lag fuse, series in the line path
line_fed_switch_short.why_it_can: it is a series, self-interrupting element present in every line-fed path, including the active bridge's line terminals, and it melts on I2t and extinguishes at current zero
line_fed_switch_short.why_it_is_not_yet_relied_on: total clearing behaviour at the prospective fault current and matching test conditions is UNESTABLISHED; only a typical melting I2t of 1638 A2s at 10x rated and a 160 A breaking capacity at 250 VAC are published, and the prospective current itself is unknown because the line impedance is unresolved
line_fed_switch_short.cannot_be_assisted_by: active-bridge gate shutdown (gates off leaves the body diodes conducting)

internal_capacitor_discharge.why_nothing_acts: no element with an interrupting function lies in this loop: F1 is outside it, the shunt U12 has one terminal on it, the PFC controller cannot sense it, and gate shutdown cannot open a shorted U10 or a conducting U9
internal_capacitor_discharge.conclusion: No adequate protection exists on the current board for the internal capacitor-discharge loop.
internal_capacitor_discharge.crowbar_note: a DC-bus crowbar would DIVERT the discharge, not interrupt it; it needs a coordinated series interruption or an energy-handling path and a trigger, none of which exists today

faults_it_cannot_interrupt: internal capacitor discharge: nothing acts, and gate shutdown / shunt U12 / F1 / the PFC controller are all outside the loop
any already-bolted short: gate shutdown cannot open a physical short, and an OFF active bridge still conducts through its body diodes
a crowbar alone (without a coordinated series interruption or energy-handling path) diverts but does not interrupt
a line-fed fault below F1's clearing threshold can persist past the device SOA even though F1 is topologically in the path
L-PE / common-mode surge: the MOV is line-to-neutral only, and the active bridge's L/R nodes see only the L-N clamp
active-bridge cross-conduction or shoot-through from a shorted device: no detection in the TEA2209T

loop_consistency.checker: zapote-erc::fault_loop via zapote-fault-loop, wrapped by zapote/tools/check_fault_loop.py
loop_consistency.scope_disclaimer: necessary connectivity check only; it does not prove a conductive path, a device state, a direction, or a distribution. A passing run is not physical evidence.

withdrawn_negative_control.role: retained negative control; not a model of this attempt

circuit_recommendation.for_the_internal_discharge_loop: Add a DC-rated, semiconductor-grade interrupting element IN series with the internal discharge path (in the bus between the capacitor bank and the boost diode/switch junction), coordinated to carry the steady bus current (~4.5 A at ~1796 W / 400 V) and to clear the ~100 us multi-kA pulse; OR a DC-bus crowbar PLUS a coordinated series interruption and energy-handling path. A bus capacitor is not a protection element.
circuit_recommendation.for_the_line_fed_loop: Establish F1's total clearing behaviour at the actual prospective current and matching test conditions and confirm it clears inside the surviving devices' SOA; if it does not, add a faster line-side element or an active overcurrent trip WITH a series interrupter. An overcurrent trip alone cannot open a body-diode path.
circuit_recommendation.for_the_active_bridge: Do not credit the TEA2209T with fault interruption: it has no overcurrent protection and gate shutdown leaves the body diodes conducting. Treat the active bridge as line-fed-fault-exposed and dependent on F1 exactly as the passive bridge was.

remaining_evidence_requirements: AC source/line impedance at the fault (gating)
F1 total clearing I2t / time-current curves at the applicable voltage and prospective current (matching test conditions, not melting I2t at 10x)
internal-loop high-current impedance model: C3D20065D Vf(I), U9 Rds(Tj), bank ESR, layout
active-bridge SOA / Zth curves digitised and mapped to the actual fault waveform
MOV clamp at the specified surge waveform (AR-MOV) - gates the active-bridge voltage rating
U9 gate state at the fault instant (is the internal discharge path armed?)
